# CANDIDATE: VOLUME_SPIKE_AFTER_LOW_VIX_PULLBACK_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

After a period of low VIX (<14) causing volatility compression, a sudden volume surge on a pullback to the 20-period EMA signals institutional buying and a short‑term bounce. This edge exists because low VIX periods often precede mean-reversion moves when volume confirms absorption of selling pressure at key dynamic support (EMA20), creating a high-probability long setup in SPY 0DTE puts (via bearish structure) or calls (if bullish confirmation exists, though OP-16 focuses on bearish anchors).

## Mechanism

Entry: If VIX < 14 for the prior 30 min AND ATR(5) < 0.5 * ATR(20) (volatility compression) AND price touches EMA20 within 0.1% (pullback) AND volume > 2x average volume of the prior 5‑minute bars (volume spike) AND the bar is bullish (close > open), go long at the close of that bar (using the appropriate 0DTE put/call based on structure; for OP-16 bearish anchors we assume put entries). Exit: chart-stop at low of the compression zone (lowest low of prior 10 min), TP1 at 2R, runner trail 20% off HWM. Regime filter: avoid choppy days where price crosses EMA20 more than 3 times in 15 min; time window restricted to 10:00‑11:30 ET.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper ~= 14% headline P&L due to 50% risk cap and 3-contract minimum.
2. **Sample bias:** Proposed trigger relies on VIX, ATR, EMA, and volume thresholds; sample size unknown until backtest; overfit risk high due to multiple conditions (VIX <14, ATR compression, EMA20 touch, volume spike, bullish bar) potentially curve-fitting to noise.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward held-out window performed yet).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no validation of top 3 J days against realistic OPRA slips/spreads).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: whipsaw in low-VIX environment (e.g., VIX <14 but no follow-through volume, leading to stop-out); max drawdown: consecutive losses if compression zone fails repeatedly; blow-up scenario: volatility expansion after entry (VIX spike) causing gap-through of chart stop.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to determine if top-5 days drive X% of P&L.
